findings.affected_surface: Ruby public API — Time.xmlschema / Time.iso8601 / Time.rfc3339
findings.old_behavior: Time.xmlschema (and its aliases Time.iso8601, Time.rfc3339) passes the raw time string argument directly to internal constructor new(time). When the input string contains leading or trailing whitespace (space, tab, etc.), the regex pattern match succeeds (the pattern has \A\s*...\s*\z anchors), but the underlying new(time) call receives the whitespace-padded string and either raises ArgumentError or produces incorrect/unexpected Time object.
findings.new_behavior: Time.xmlschema (and aliases) calls time.strip on the input string before passing it to new(). Leading and trailing whitespace (spaces, tabs, etc.) are removed, and the cleaned string is correctly parsed into the expected Time object.
findings.compatibility_reason: The input contract of Time.xmlschema, Time.iso8601, and Time.rfc3339 has been relaxed. Strings with leading/trailing whitespace that previously caused an ArgumentError (or incorrect parsing) are now silently accepted and correctly parsed. Code that manually strips whitespace before these calls is now redundant (no functional breakage, but the error path changed). More importantly, code that depended on the ArgumentError being raised for whitespace-padded inputs will now silently get a Time object instead, potentially masking bugs. This affects all callers of these three public class methods on Time.

evidence.snippet:
if pattern.match?(time)
          new(time.strip)    # was: new(time)
        else
          raise ArgumentError.new("invalid xmlschema format: #{time.inspect}")
        end

def xmlschema(time)
      pattern = /\A\s*...\s*\z/ix
      _xmlschema(pattern, time)
    end
    alias iso8601 xmlschema

    def rfc3339(time)
      pattern = /\A\s*...\s*\z/ix
      _xmlschema(pattern, time)
    end

findings.why_not_internal_only: Time.xmlschema, Time.iso8601, and Time.rfc3339 are public class methods on the core Time class, part of Ruby's standard library public API. The change is in the private helper _xmlschema but directly affects the observable behavior of all three public entry points.
findings.uncertainty: The exact failure mode of the old code (ArgumentError vs incorrect Time object) depends on Ruby version (>= 3.2) and how Time.new handles whitespace-padded ISO 8601 strings, which may vary. However, the behavioral change is unambiguous: output for whitespace-padded inputs differs before/after the patch.
findings.recommended_review: Verify that no production code depends on Time.xmlschema raising ArgumentError for whitespace-padded strings as a validation mechanism.
findings.test_recommendation: Write directed tests for Time.xmlschema, Time.iso8601, and Time.rfc3339 with various leading/trailing whitespace patterns: spaces, tabs, mixed whitespace, edge cases like entirely whitespace strings. Verify old behavior (ArgumentError for whitespace-padded) vs new behavior (correct parsing).
